rubrics.criterion: Every update of the wire-activity accounting record in the packet sources is now expressed as a call into the module that owns the record (the statistics helper pair), so no packet-layer function maintains the record's fields inline anymore.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central obligation of the task prompt: the record's maintenance must have one home. This case scattered 53 direct field-update statements across 18 packet functions over 10 source files, so the grader should confirm the consolidation, not a partial conversion.

rubrics.criterion: The delegated accounting preserves what the report shows today: for identical packet traffic the record still reflects the same per-type send/receive counts, wire byte totals, payload byte totals with the same high-water behavior, session starts plus the session-scoped reset on connect (without clearing lifetime reject totals), rejected packets, accepted frames from both read paths, decoded topic-entry counts, and the last-inspected packet type.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt's compatibility boundary is that support dumps must show exactly the same numbers; a delegation that changes any accounting value is a regression of the feature the task exists to preserve.

rubrics.criterion: The owning module's public API carries the facts the packet flows produce: entry points and parameters exist for facts the original narrow entry point (direction, packet type, wire length) could not express, such as payload length, list multiplicity, rejection, framing, session lifecycle, and inspected type.
rubrics.rationale: The original one-entry-point API was the root cause of the scatter; a repair that does not widen it forces the next accounting request to be carved into packet code again.

rubrics.criterion: None of the functions that carried inline record maintenance still updates the record directly (including write, increment, or handing the record elsewhere). The hidden locations to verify are: MQTTSerialize_connect, MQTTDeserialize_connack, MQTTSerialize_zero (MQTTConnectClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_connect (MQTTConnectServer.c); MQTTSerialize_publish and MQTTDeserialize_ack's reject branch (MQTTSerializePublish.c, MQTTDeserializePublish.c); MQTTDeserialize_publish (MQTTDeserializePublish.c); MQTTSerialize_subscribe and MQTTDeserialize_suback (MQTTSubscribeClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_subscribe and MQTTSerialize_suback (MQTTSubscribeServer.c); MQTTSerialize_unsubscribe (MQTTUnsubscribeClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe and MQTTSerialize_unsuback (MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c); MQTTPacket_read and MQTTPacket_readnb (MQTTPacket.c); MQTTFormat_toClientString and MQTTFormat_toServerString (MQTTFormat.c).
rubrics.rationale: The scattered sites are the instance's responsibility manifest; each one left inline means a future accounting change still needs a multi-file edit, which is the failure the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The change does not fix the spread by discarding the accounting: the record is not left unmaintained for flows that maintained it before (for example, simply deleting the inline statements and leaving the record reading zero, or gutting the module so nothing flows into it).
rubrics.rationale: Blanket deletion silences the maintenance spread while destroying the support-dump feature the prompt explicitly requires to keep working; this is the most tempting shortcut for this instance and must be graded as a failure.

rubrics.criterion: Every flow family that fed the record before the change still feeds it after: the connect lifecycle (session reset and session starts, connack, the shared zero-length/keep-alive path), publish in both directions with payload volume and high-water, subscribe/unsubscribe and their confirmations on both client and server sides, inbound server-side connect, rejected packets on truncated-input paths, accepted frames from both the blocking and the non-blocking read paths, and both operator formatting views.
rubrics.rationale: The instances of this case hide across ten files in deliberately different shapes; a repair that converts the easy families and drops a quiet one (the non-blocking read or a formatting view are the likely casualties) leaves the report lying about part of the wire activity.

rubrics.criterion: Ownership stays coherent after the change: the record and all its update entry points live in the single statistics module source pair, and no bookkeeping helper that updates the record was introduced separately inside individual consumer files (which would re-create the scattered policy in a new shape).
rubrics.rationale: The task asks for one home for the accounting policy; per-file wrappers would reintroduce the same multi-file maintenance cost for the next accounting change.

rubrics.criterion: The change does not introduce a second shared record, a parallel counter set, or per-module copies of any accounting field that would have to be kept in sync alongside the original record.
rubrics.rationale: Duplicating state is the classic false resolution for this kind of consolidation: it makes each copy look clean while multiplying the places a future accounting change must touch.

rubrics.criterion: No debris of the inline maintenance remains in the affected functions: scratch declarations that existed only to support it (for example, a loop index declared solely to clear the counters), leftover comment lines describing the old inline bookkeeping, dead branches left by removing it, and no consumer file keeps a mention of the owning module that it no longer references.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state added local scaffolding around the record updates (most notably a loop index used only by the session-reset loop in the connect serializer); a careful consolidation removes the scaffolding with the code it supported, together with any include that existed only for it.

rubrics.criterion: The statistics module exposes no dead public surface after the change: every public entry point it declares has at least one calling site in the packet sources (the original narrow entry point is fine to keep if the conforming fixed-length ack serializer still calls it).
rubrics.rationale: Rewiring eighteen sites through new, richer entry points can strand the module's original API; leftover uncalled entry points are exactly the kind of obsolete artifact this case's cleanup category should catch.

rubrics.criterion: The packet layer's externally observable behavior is unchanged: serialized byte layouts, public function signatures, and return codes of every serializer, deserializer, and read path are the same as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: The accounting is diagnostic-only plumbing in an embedded protocol library; any byte-level or API-level change breaks wire compatibility for every consumer, which the prompt forbids.

rubrics.criterion: No accounting value moved to a different event than the one it describes: a packet is not counted twice for the same wire traffic (for example by accounting at both a caller and a callee), rejected packets are not tallied as received, the session reset does not clear lifetime counters (reject totals, session starts), the non-blocking completion is not counted at the wrong state-machine transition, and the inspected-type viewport is not captured for only one of the two formatting views.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete drift modes this instance's sites make possible, because every family has its own update point and its own error path; a relocation that changes which event updates the record silently corrupts support dumps.

rubrics.criterion: The packet layer remains suitable for small embedded targets: the delegation introduces no dynamic allocation and no new static buffers, and the per-packet bookkeeping stays constant-time relative to packet and list sizes (no new scanning of the record or buffers on hot paths).
rubrics.rationale: This codebase targets bare-metal and small-footprint deployments, which the prompt calls out; a repair that adds allocations or heavier per-loop work trades one problem for another.
